role.altitude: The crusher and grinder operator keeps watching the line, judging product and machine condition, rejecting product and readjusting gaps and feeds; reading local gauges, finding the supervisor for every repair and filling paper production forms shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading the control screen and trends
Entering tests and downtime on the tablet
role.ambitious_version: An operator whose forms fill themselves and who spends the shift at the machines.

tasks.short: Walk the line and observe operation of equipment, check loads, temperatures and flows, and judge continuity of flow, safety and efficient operation to detect malfunctions.

steps.what: Operator walks the line and observes feed, crushers and conveyors
Operator checks motor load, bearing temperature and flow rates on local gauges
Operator judges whether operation is normal and detects malfunctions

tasks.design: Motor current, throughput, bearing temperature and vibration are shown on the control screen with alarm limits, so the operator reads them in one place instead of at each machine, and walks the line for what only eyes, ears and nose catch: spillage, blockages, noise and smell. Walking the line and judging operation stay with the operator. Safety stops stay hard-wired; no learning model takes part in them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were only on local gauges.
tasks.enabler_now: Sensors on motors and bearings shown on the control screen.
tasks.still_hard: Blockages that build up slowly between rounds.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a change in the crusher's sound before an alarm.
tasks.altitude: Fewer gauges to read; watching stays.

evidence.claim: Learning models in safety functions of machinery need third-party conformity assessment, so they stay out of stops and guards.
Motor and bearing sensors can feed control screens with alarm limits.

assumptions: Boundary: observing operation; recording data (task 12378) and notifying repairs (task 12382) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1 and s2: sensors on the main motors and bearings wired to the control system, about 60% of readings; s2 is priced at that share.
Walking the line and judging keep their full time; s2 keeps 50 because about 60% of the gauge readings move to the control screen and the rest are still read at the machine.
research_questions: Are malfunctions caught before damage more often?

incremental.description: Operator reports sensors that read wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an older line where sensors cover only a quarter of the readings (3.5); high: about 60% of readings on the control screen as assumed (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide that a repair is needed, notify supervisors of needed repairs, and record the repair request.

steps.what: Operator decides that a repair is needed
Operator notifies the supervisor and explains the needed repair
Operator writes the repair request: in the paper log today; on the tablet with the scanned equipment tag, a fault from the list and a short note after the change
Operator takes a photo of the fault on the tablet, showing the equipment and no people
Operator checks the final request: equipment, fault described, photo without people and urgency
Operator submits the checked request to the supervisor and maintenance

tasks.design: For non-urgent repairs the operator writes a request on the tablet with the equipment tag, a fault from the list, a note and a photo, checks it and submits it once; it reaches the supervisor and maintenance at once, instead of the operator finding the supervisor and writing in a paper log. Urgent faults are still reported by radio straight away. Deciding a repair is needed stays with the operator.

approvals.approved_version: The repair request with equipment tag, fault, note, photo and urgency exactly as checked by the operator in s3b, submitted once to the supervisor's and maintenance's request list in the maintenance app; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Requests went by word of mouth and a paper log.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance apps with equipment tags and photo requests.
tasks.still_hard: Faults that need the supervisor to see them in person.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a noise means stop now.
tasks.altitude: Less walking and writing; deciding stays.

reach.learn: Whether requests arrive complete with photos.

evidence.claim: Machine data and tablet forms going straight into MES or a historian remove re-keyed paper sheets.

assumptions: Boundary: notifying repairs; observing equipment (task 12376) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2 and s3: about 70% of repair needs are non-urgent and go through the tablet; s2 is priced at that share.

Deciding, the photo, the check and the submit keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because urgent faults still go by radio and the supervisor still asks about many requests; s3 keeps 85 because the request is still written and only the equipment details come from the tag.

incremental.description: Operator reports missing equipment tags in the app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many faults are urgent or need the supervisor on site, so most notifications stay in person and the request saves nothing (5.7); high: about 70% of repairs non-urgent as assumed (19.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record machine readings, test results and production counts and downtime from operations, testing and production on specified forms, review and sign the shift record, and hand in the forms.

steps.what: Operator records machine readings and throughput on the form
Operator records test results: particle size and moisture, on the paper form today and on the tablet form with limits after the change
Operator records production counts, downtime and reasons
Operator reviews the shift record: readings, test results, counts and downtime reasons against the shift
Operator signs the reviewed shift record on the tablet into the production system
Operator hands in the paper forms at the office

tasks.design: Machine readings and throughput from the scale and the control system go into the production system automatically at set times, so the operator only checks them. Test results are still entered by the operator, on a tablet form with limits that flag out-of-spec values. Production counts come from the scale, and downtime is captured from machine stops with the operator picking a reason. The operator reviews the shift record and signs it once on the tablet, and nothing is handed in on paper. Per-operator records are used for production only; any other use is agreed with the works council first.

approvals.approved_version: The shift record with readings, test results, counts and downtime reasons exactly as reviewed by the operator in s4, signed once on the tablet into the production system; any change needs a new review and signature.

tasks.previous_blocker: Paper forms filled by hand and re-keyed by the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine data in production systems and tablet forms.
tasks.human_edge: Writing the remark that explains an odd reading.

ambition.what: Spot drifting particle size within the shift from live data.

reach.learn: Whether test data arrive the same shift.

evidence.claim: Per-operator production logs can monitor staff and need works council consent.
Machine data and tablet forms going straight into production systems remove re-keyed paper sheets.

assumptions: Boundary: recording data; reading work orders (task 12375) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1 and s3: scale and control system linked to the production system for the main line.

Review, signature and test results keep their full time; test results are the operator's own first records. s1 keeps 15 for checking the sent values; s3 keeps 40 because downtime reasons are still entered.
unknowns: Share of machines with data links.
research_questions: Are production data complete and on time?

incremental.description: Operator reports wrong machine data and missing downtime reasons.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the machines are older ones without data links, so their readings and counts are still written (29.0); high: main line fully linked (48.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect product samples, decide to reject defective products, divert them, and readjust equipment to eliminate problems.

steps.what: Operator inspects product samples: size, texture and colour
Operator decides to reject defective product
Operator diverts or removes the defective product
Operator readjusts equipment: gap settings, speed and feed

tasks.design: Where an inline particle-size analyser is installed, its trend on the control screen shows drift between samples, so the operator takes fewer hand samples and still checks texture and colour by eye. Deciding to reject, diverting and readjusting stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quality was only known from hand samples.
tasks.still_hard: Defects in colour or texture that no analyser measures.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling from the product that the liners are worn.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; judging and adjusting stay.

evidence.claim: Inline analysers measure particle size continuously.
Sorting good from bad product is not a safety function under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: rejecting product and readjusting; recording test results (task 12378) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: an inline analyser on the main line only; s1 is priced at that share.
Deciding, diverting and readjusting keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the line has an inline analyser.

incremental.description: Operator checks the analyser against a hand sample each shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the analyser drifts or is often down, so hand samples stay nearly as frequent (1.4); high: main line with a working analyser as assumed (6.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
